subject: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ops@skyapp.io
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vendor-admin@vendorops.com
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook

Hi SkyApp team —

Quick context: SkyApp's onboarding hit a snag during PO issuance. The procurement system generated PO-78431 but the line items were split and some SKU quantities got duplicated in the ledger. Because of the mismatch, a temporary spend cap hold was applied this morning while we confirm the correct mapping.

I've attached an export of the PO issuance log that shows the timestamped events (po_issuance_log_20260913.csv). Can you please confirm the following by EOD Monday?

- Which PO should be canonical for SkyApp (PO-78431 vs PO-78431-A)?
- For each SKU in the attached sheet, confirm intended quantity and unit price. We flagged SKU-ALPHA-01 and SKU-BETA-02 as inconsistent.
- Any internal vendor reference numbers that should map back to our PO field (VendorRef / OrderRef).

Procurement ask: once you confirm the canonical PO and corrected quantities we'll lift the temporary spend cap (currently at $45k) so CloudOps can provision capacity. If you prefer, attach a corrected line-item file (xlsx) and we will ingest it and push the ledger change through our provisioning pipeline.

CC'ing Kimberly (billing) and Neha (vendor ops) so we can coordinate the correction and the short-lived funding hold. Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation so we can avoid stalled provisioning.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: po_issuance_log_20260913.csv (CSV export, 78 rows)

From: ops@skyapp.io
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: vendor-admin@vendorops.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up and the export. We pulled the log and reproduced the behavior — the fulfillment system produced PO-78431 and, on an internal retry, created a follow-on aggregation PO-78431-A which duplicated two line items. Apologies for the noise.

Summary of our findings:
- Canonical PO: PO-78431 (please use this for billing).
- Duplicate lines: SKU-ALPHA-01 appears twice (qty 10 and qty 0 in a retry stub). Effective qty should be 10.
- Mismatched price: SKU-BETA-02 unit price was overridden by a promotion rule; correct unit is $1,250.00.
- VendorRef: SkyRef-9932 should be used for all items.

We're attaching a corrected lineitem_corrections_20260914.xlsx that lists the canonical rows and the delta corrections. Let us know if you want us to re-submit via your vendor portal or simply provide the corrected file for you to ingest.

Regards,
Maya R. (Operations Lead)
SkyApp Inc.

Attachments: lineitem_corrections_20260914.xlsx (XLSX, 1 worksheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ops@skyapp.io
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:02 -0700
Subject: Re: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook

Jonas / Maya —

This is good — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of operational notes from billing:

- If we lift the spend cap before the correction is ingested, CloudOps will provision but finance will still require a handoff ticket for reconciliation. I prefer to lift the cap after ingestion and quick verification (10–15m spot check).
- Please confirm the corrected total not to exceed $48,000 after the price normalization (we'll approve lifting the cap up to that.)
- Once ingested, please attach the ingestion ticket number back into this thread.

If SkyApp can re-submit through the vendor portal (preferred), Neha can take the ingestion step immediately; otherwise Jonas can ingest the attached xlsx.

K

Kimberly Park
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: vendor-admin@vendorops.com
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ops@skyapp.io
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:17 -0700
Subject: Re: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook

Hi all —

VendorOps processed the corrected spreadsheet and created ingestion ticket ING-9347. Changes applied:
- Merged PO-78431-A into PO-78431 (duplicates removed).
- SKU-ALPHA-01 consolidated to qty 10.
- SKU-BETA-02 price corrected to $1,250.00.
- VendorRef set to SkyRef-9932 on all lines.

We held the ledger change in pending until Redwood confirms. Current post-correction estimated spend is $46,750 which is within Kimberly's $48,000 threshold.

Ticket: ING-9347
Provisioning can proceed once Redwood lifts the temporary spend cap.

Regards,
Saleh (VendorOps - Intake)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ops@skyapp.io, vendor-admin@vendorops.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO issuance log, spend cap hold, and line-item remediation playbook

Thanks team —

Confirmed: ING-9347 looks correct, SkyRef-9932 mapped, and total after corrections $46,750. Kimberly, please lift the temporary spend cap to $48,000 and notify CloudOps to proceed with provisioning.

Neha — please mark the vendor record with a remediation note and set the onboarding status to ACTIVE. VendorOps / SkyApp — please note the canonical PO is PO-78431 for future invoices.

Closing this thread after provisioning completes; keep the Jira PROC-4122 updated with any reconciliation variance.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
